candidateSources.layerA: arXiv official /new batch for Wednesday 7 October 2026 (cs.AI, cs.CL, cs.MA new-submissions + cross-listed sections fetched via arXiv listing pages; replacement-submission entries excluded). 436 unique new/cross-listed arxiv IDs identified across the three categories; after filtering to the 2610.* prefix (434 ids) and fetching full title+abstract metadata in 13 batched arXiv export-API queries, a title+abstract keyword triage (agent/agentic/multi-agent in title, or tool-use/RAG/memory/harness/jailbreak/guardrail/autonomous combined with llm/language-model in text) retained 111 agent-relevant candidates. Of these, ~19 were shortlisted for closer abstract-level review given a strong recurring theme (agent memory governance, agent evaluation trust, agent safety-gate composition); the 3 most promising were read in full body (methods/results/limitations) via arxiv.org/html for the credibility-gate assessment.
layerB: HuggingFace Daily Papers API (huggingface.co/api/daily_papers) for 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-07 — cross-checked against the 434 Layer-A candidate IDs. 4 matches found; of these only 2610.07753 ('From Evidence to Action: How Tool-Using Agents Fail') and 2610.08463 ('UNREAL: Unifying Retrieval and Long-Context with a Single Model') are on-topic (the other 2 matches are general LLM training/distillation papers, off-topic). Both used as community-signal evidence in their respective watch entries; neither was selected given stronger-competitor coverage of their angles by the selected trio.

Groundlane web_search 'site:huggingface.co/papers OR site:paperswithcode.com' targeted check for the three selected arxiv IDs (2610.07309, 2610.07274, 2610.07359) — no hits for any of the three, confirming no HF Daily Papers or Papers with Code pickup yet (consistent with all three being 2 days old).

Semantic Scholar per-paper lookup (api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/ARXIV:{id}) — succeeded for 2610.07274 (citationCount 0, no venue) and 2610.07359 (citationCount 0, no venue, author name confirmed as Cheng-Lin Yang). Calls for 2610.07309 returned persistent HTTP 429 across multiple retries; citationCount for that paper is reported as 'presumed 0, Semantic Scholar unconfirmed' based on paper age (2 days). toolDegradation recorded.
candidateSources.layerC: 14-day lookback window 2026-09-24 to 2026-10-07 across .research/daily-arxiv-screening/*.json, excluding IDs already in seen-arxiv-ids.txt. Found 131 distinct watch/rejected(stronger-competitor)/rejected(evidence-insufficient) entries in that window, heavily dominated by a recurring 'agent harness optimization' and 'agent memory benchmark' cluster (e.g. ActiveSaddler, Causal Memory Policy, DeFA, MCRI, Argo-Bench) carried forward across many days. Given decay(d)=0.85^d strongly favors same-day candidates and today's Layer A batch surfaced an unusually strong, cohesive fresh theme (agent memory admissibility / evaluation trust / safety-gate composition, all submitted 2026-10-05/06), individual re-verification of the full 131-item backlog was not repeated this round — consistent with prior days' stated practice when Layer A/B are already strong. No new code-release, replication, or venue-upgrade signal was observed in today's Layer A/B searches that would specifically trigger pulling forward any Layer C item over today's selections.

candidates.title: The Right Memory in the Wrong Context: Verifying Retrieval Admissibility in Long-Term Agent Memory
candidates.venue: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop "Who Verifies the Agents? Toward Reliable Agent Development"
candidates.institution: University of Arkansas at Little Rock
credibilityEvidence: Section 4: post-hoc reanalysis of 3,767 queries across RHELM+MemOps public benchmarks with matched-recall route comparison
16 controlled exposure scenarios with reader-specific 95% CIs
Limitations section explicitly scopes what is and isn't established
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Core metrics, baselines, and bounded-case diagnostics are covered across two independent public benchmarks, but authors explicitly limit claims to two sources and 7 RHELM groups, not safety certification or model ranking
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Numbers are concrete and limitations disclosed honestly, but only 1 of 16 exposure-scenario CIs excludes zero, so the core safety claim rests on a small effect
candidates.primaryLimitation: Narrow evaluation scope (2 public sources, 7 RHELM groups); namespaces assumed trustworthy rather than independently verified; does not cover graph-structured memory selectors
candidates.presentationReason: Method, formal framework, experimental scope, and limitations are clearly delineated with explicit boundary statements
candidates.reason: Strongest and most rigorous of today's memory-governance cluster: larger, cross-benchmark evaluation with formal three-status framework, NeurIPS workshop acceptance, and the most honest/explicit limitations statement among the candidates in this cluster.

candidates.title: A Trust Layer for Agent Evaluation
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint (not peer-reviewed; code withheld until acceptance)
credibilityEvidence: Section 4: tested on 5 agent configurations across ALE's 3 difficulty tiers and 11 domains
Limitations section states sample size (13-20 passes/config) and single-benchmark scope explicitly
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Validated on only one benchmark (Agents' Last Exam); authors state the result establishes 'most passes fail a check', not a ranking of agents
reproducibilityEvidence: Method and ALE benchmark are public; code explicitly withheld until paper acceptance
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Concrete, specific numbers (22.6% pass rate, 95% CI) with explicit acknowledgment of single-benchmark scope and small per-configuration sample
candidates.primaryLimitation: Validated on only one benchmark (ALE); core finding is about trustworthiness of passes in aggregate, not a ranking of which agent is stronger
candidates.presentationReason: Four verification dimensions, their evidentiary basis, and scope boundaries are explicitly and clearly stated
candidates.reason: Directly challenges the industry-wide assumption that a benchmark 'pass' equals trustworthy evidence of capability, with a concrete and alarming number (22.6%) from a real benchmark; complements the memory and safety-gate selections by covering the evaluation-infrastructure angle.

candidates.title: Evaluate the Stack, Not the Layer: Do Deterministic and LLM Gates for Agent Actions Fail Independently?
candidates.citationVelocity: presumed near 0, Semantic Scholar unconfirmed (persistent HTTP 429 on lookup)
candidates.institution: Not listed; presumed independent researcher (sole author, personal GitHub username)
credibilityEvidence: Phi-correlation and CI-based quantification of n_mult (effective layer count) across 1,119 labelled actions from 3 corpora
Honest report of a methodological incident (unrequested model version served in 50/112 batches, overturning a pre-declared analysis rule and reversing 5 conclusions, both versions reported)
Ethical Considerations and Limitations sections explicit about scope (no adaptive adversary)
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Tested on one stack configuration across three corpora without an adaptive adversary; author explicitly flags this scope limit
reproducibilityEvidence: Data, scripts, and provenance fully released on GitHub
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Statistically rigorous (significance tested per pair) and transparent about an incident affecting results, but no adaptive-adversary testing narrows the claim's real-world security scope
candidates.primaryLimitation: No adaptive adversary tested; one corpus's judge layer was accidentally served an unrequested model version for part of the study
candidates.presentationReason: Despite dense statistical notation, the core claim, evidence, and scope boundaries (including the self-reported incident) are stated plainly
candidates.reason: Directly and quantitatively tests the 'more layers = more safety' assumption underlying agent guardrail architecture with a novel, falsifiable 'effective layer count' metric and full public artifacts; completes the trio's coverage of a third distinct agent-infrastructure component (safety gates, alongside memory and evaluation).

candidates.title: AgentMemGate: Addressing Speculation Contamination in Conversational Assistant Memory
credibilityEvidence: Abstract reports concrete numbers (87.5% to 0% contamination elimination, 65% to 95% task accuracy) and a 147-conversation held-out set; not read in full body
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Abstract-level only; full method/results/limitations not read this round
reproducibilityEvidence: Authors state datasets, prompts, and evaluation code are released
candidates.reason: Same memory-governance theme as selected 2610.07309, but narrower scope (single write-time gate mechanism on one assistant's profile store vs. 07309's cross-benchmark admissibility framework spanning retrieval, exposure, and disclosure); kept as watch-equivalent in case 07309's angle is exhausted in a future round.

candidates.title: When to Remember, When to Abstain: Category-Conditioned Retention for Reliable Agent Memory
candidates.venue: NeurIPS 2026 Social Agent Workshop (4-page extended abstract)
credibilityEvidence: Abstract reports a deployed cold-start pipeline test on 100 synthetic personas with 4,715 candidate assertions; effect size is self-described as 'modest but consistent'
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: 4-page workshop extended abstract; smallest and most modest effect size (~36% relative reduction) of the memory-governance cluster
candidates.reason: Thinnest evidence (4-page extended abstract, synthetic personas only) and smallest effect size among today's memory-governance candidates; 07309 covers the same general problem space with a much larger, cross-benchmark evaluation.

candidates.title: From Evidence to Action: How Tool-Using Agents Fail
credibilityEvidence: Abstract describes a new benchmark (SafeActBench, 656 cases, six domains, five protocols) and ten model-harness configurations; not read in full body
candidates.reason: Has real community signal (HF Daily Papers pick) and solid apparent scale (656-case new benchmark), but its angle (tool-use failure taxonomy) substantially overlaps the evaluation-trust angle already covered by selected 2610.07274 and the safety-gate angle covered by 2610.07359; including it would have made the trio redundant rather than covering distinct angles. Worth revisiting in Layer C lookback if the selected trio's angles are exhausted.

candidates.title: Transect: Retaining Observability for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Evaluations
communitySignals: Open-source tool built on Inspect Scout
credibilityEvidence: Abstract describes an open-source transcript-analysis tool demonstrated on a ~13M-token AI R&D evaluation; primarily a tooling contribution rather than a research finding
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Single demonstration case study on one evaluation run; not a controlled multi-case study
candidates.reason: A useful engineering tool but reads more as a tool-recommendation candidate than a research-finding digest entry; single case-study demonstration is thinner evidence than the selected trio's multi-corpus/multi-benchmark evaluations. Better suited to the daily-digest-tool routine.

candidates.title: Where Rules End and Judges Begin: Measuring the Judgment Boundary in Multi-Agent Systems Security
credibilityEvidence: Abstract describes a 5-principle defense framework (DEFER1) with a 28-check cascade; not read in full body
candidates.reason: Same safety-gate-composition theme as selected 2610.07359, but proposes a new defense cascade rather than testing the standard composition assumption empirically; 07359's falsifiable 'effective layer count' metric is the more novel and directly relevant contribution for today's theme.

candidates.title: POLAR: Ontology-Guided Risk Prevention for Tool-Calling LLM Agents
candidates.reason: Another pre-emptive tool-call guardrail proposal; overlaps with today's safety-gate theme but proposes a new mechanism rather than testing the composition assumption; 07359 is the stronger, more novel fit for today's angle.

candidates.title: APEX: Active Protection at Execution Boundaries for LLM Agents
candidates.reason: A new indirect-prompt-injection defense mechanism; overlaps the safety-gate theme but 07359's empirical composition-testing contribution is more novel and relevant for today's selection.

candidates.title: Trust-Gated Capability Control: Breaking the Trust-Vulnerability Paradox in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
candidates.reason: A conceptual trust-stack proposal for multi-agent systems; adjacent to today's theme but less directly a test of an existing assumption than the selected trio.

candidates.title: Semantic Behavioral Watermarking: Paraphrase-Robust and Forgery-Resistant Provenance for LLM Agents
candidates.reason: Provenance/watermarking rather than reliability verification of memory, evaluation, or safety gates; off-topic relative to today's theme despite being agent-adjacent.

candidates.title: Beyond Corrected Memory: Execution Consistency in Multi-Agent Systems
candidates.reason: Conceptually adjacent to the memory-governance theme (correct records != sufficient for task duties) but abstract alone doesn't establish evidence strength relative to 07309; worth a closer read in a future round if the theme recurs.

candidates.title: MINDSET: Energy-based Schema Evolution for Long Conversational Agent Memory
candidates.reason: Memory-schema-evolution angle differs from retention/admissibility focus of selected 07309; not deep-read this round given time budget, kept for Layer C reconsideration.

candidates.title: DAEDALUS: Bootstrapping Agent Memory from Self-Generated Tasks
candidates.reason: About building procedural memory from self-play rather than verifying whether existing memory is admissible/trustworthy; different angle from today's selected theme, kept for future consideration.

candidates.title: Memory Depth and Reconstructed Context Width: A Controlled Evaluation of Hierarchical Retrieval
candidates.reason: A hyperparameter/architecture study (depth vs. context width) rather than a trust/admissibility verification; different angle from today's theme, kept for future consideration.

candidates.title: MemCo: Memory-Centric Collaboration for Generalizing LLM Agents to Unseen Environments
candidates.reason: About shared-memory generalization across environments, a capability angle rather than a trust/verification angle; different from today's selected theme, kept for future consideration.

candidates.title: Auditable Claims about AI Agents
credibilityEvidence: Abstract states the core contribution as a one-sentence position/argument tied to EU AI Act Article 12, not an empirical study
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Position paper; no experiments to assess
candidates.reason: Pure position paper (per selection standard, position papers can serve as trend background but are not main daily selections unless the event itself is highly impactful); thematically relevant as background context for the trust-verification theme but does not provide empirical evidence of its own.

candidates.title: UNREAL: Unifying Retrieval and Long-Context with a Single Model
credibilityEvidence: Abstract reports strong, specific recall gains (e.g. HotpotQA 49.1% to 73.2%) across multiple benchmarks; not read in full body
candidates.reason: Strong apparent results and real community signal (HF Daily Papers pick), but reads as an IR/long-context architecture paper rather than a direct agent-infrastructure trust/verification finding; doesn't fit today's cohesive theme as well as the selected trio. Worth a closer look as a RAG/retrieval-architecture candidate on a future day.
